```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(targets)

tar_source(here::here("R"))
source(here::here("reports", "_thesis_setup.R"))

tar_load(c(
  area_shp, stroke_centres, stroke_times, stroke_area, diag_stroke,
  smr_geo_full, smr_geo_tracer, smr_geo_allage, C_matrix,
  control_fits, control_table, control_diagnostics,
  stroke_times_table, exposure_contrast_table, tracer_per_10min,
  tracer_engine_table, tracer_exposure_table,
  outcome_feasibility_table, allage_table, allage_diagnostics,
  mort_raw
))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this report is for

The main results document reports the tracer coefficient. This one asks the
prior question: **could this design have detected an effect if one existed?**
A null coefficient from an exposure with no contrast, or from an outcome the
exposure cannot plausibly move, is not evidence of no effect — and the two are
indistinguishable in a coefficient table.
:::

# 1. The stroke network

## 1.1 Centres, for verification

The DGR node list gives a comune, not a street address, so the coordinate is
the address for checking purposes. **Open a few of the map links** — especially
any row whose `source` is not the regional registry. A facility resolved to the
wrong side of a city silently changes the catchment of every area around it,
and no automated check will catch it.

```{r centre-table}
stroke_centre_table(stroke_centres) |>
  kable(col.names = c("ID", "Facility", "Level", "Ente", "Comune", "Prov.",
                      "Lat", "Lon", "Geocoded via", "Map"),
        caption = "Every accredited stroke centre used in the routing, including those outside the ATS Milano territory.")
```

```{r centre-source-summary}
sf::st_drop_geometry(stroke_centres) |>
  count(is_hub, geocode_source) |>
  mutate(is_hub = ifelse(is_hub, "Hub (SU II)", "Spoke (SU I)")) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Level", "Geocoding source", "n"),
        caption = "How each centre was located. Manual overrides and Nominatim results deserve the closest look.")
```

## 1.2 Where they are

```{r fig-centres, fig.cap="Accredited stroke centres over the study area. Centres outside the ATS Milano boundary are included in the routing because residents near the edge may be closer to them."}
plot_stroke_centres(
  area_shp, stroke_centres,
  caption = "Triangles: level-II hubs performing mechanical thrombectomy. Circles: spoke stroke units."
)
```

# 2. Where strokes are killing people

Cerebrovascular mortality, ages 0–74, 2022–2024, indirectly standardised for
age and sex. This is the tracer outcome.

```{r fig-cvd-map, fig.cap="Cerebrovascular SMR by areal unit. Hubs overlaid."}
g <- sf::st_as_sf(smr_geo_tracer)
g$cvd_smr <- g$cvd_obs / g$cvd_exp

ggplot(g) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cvd_smr), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(stroke_centres)[stroke_centres$is_hub, ],
                                  sf::st_crs(g)),
          shape = 24, fill = "#d94801", colour = "grey10", size = 2.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#8c2d04",
                       midpoint = 1, name = "SMR") +
  theme_atlas(map = TRUE)
```

## 2.1 What kind of strokes are these?

The mechanism the exposure is supposed to act through depends entirely on this
table. Thrombectomy acts on cerebral infarction (I63) alone; neurosurgical and
neurocritical care act on the haemorrhagic subtypes (I60-I62).

```{r subtype}
sub <- mort_raw |>
  mutate(key = toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", causa))) |>
  filter(startsWith(key, "I6"), eta < 75) |>
  mutate(k3 = substr(key, 1, 3),
         subtype = case_when(
           k3 == "I63"                ~ "I63 Cerebral infarction (thrombectomy)",
           k3 %in% c("I60","I61","I62") ~ "I60-I62 Haemorrhagic (neurosurgery)",
           k3 == "I64"                ~ "I64 Stroke, type not specified",
           k3 == "I69"                ~ "I69 Sequelae",
           TRUE                       ~ paste(k3, "Other cerebrovascular")
         )) |>
  count(subtype, name = "deaths") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * deaths / sum(deaths)) |>
  arrange(desc(deaths))

sub |>
  mutate(pct = fmt_pct(pct)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Subtype", "Deaths", "%"),
        caption = "Cerebrovascular deaths under 75, by subtype. Note which channel each belongs to.")
```

```{r dilution, results="asis"}
i63  <- sum(sub$deaths[grepl("^I63", sub$subtype)])
haem <- sum(sub$deaths[grepl("^I60", sub$subtype)])
tot  <- sum(sub$deaths)
lvo <- 0.20; win <- 0.50
thromb <- (i63 / tot) * lvo * win

cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "\n> **Dilution.** If the exposure acted through thrombectomy alone it could ",
  "touch %s of this outcome (%s I63 x ~%.0f%% large-vessel occlusion x ~%.0f%% ",
  "presenting in window). A 30%% mortality reduction in that subset would move ",
  "total cerebrovascular mortality by %s - far below anything this design can ",
  "resolve. Adding the neurosurgical channel (%s haemorrhagic) raises the ",
  "reachable fraction to about %s, which is the same order as the credible ",
  "interval in §5.5. **This is the argument for reframing the exposure rather ",
  "than narrowing the outcome.**\n\n"),
  fmt_pct(100*thromb), fmt_pct(100*i63/tot), 100*lvo, 100*win,
  fmt_pct(100*thromb*0.30), fmt_pct(100*haem/tot),
  fmt_pct(100*(thromb + haem/tot))))
```

```{r cvd-counts}
tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Cerebrovascular deaths, 0-74, 2022-2024",
               "Deaths per year",
               "Areal units with zero deaths",
               "Median expected count per area",
               "Areal units with expected count < 5"),
  Value = c(
    fmt_n(sum(g$cvd_obs)),
    fmt_n(sum(g$cvd_obs) / 3),
    fmt_n(sum(g$cvd_obs == 0)),
    fmt_num(median(g$cvd_exp), 1),
    fmt_n(sum(g$cvd_exp < 5))
  )
) |>
  kable(caption = "The tracer outcome. Sparse counts widen every interval that follows.")
```

# 4. Could this design detect an effect? {#sec-contrast}

::: {.callout-important}
Read this section before the coefficients. Everything in §5 is conditional on
the answer here.
:::

```{r layer-variance}
diag_stroke$layer_variance |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 2))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Layer", "n", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Max"),
        caption = "Travel-time variation within each layer of the geography. The NIL layer is the one to look at: it is 87 of the 279 units.")
```


```{r contrast}
ec <- exposure_contrast(smr_geo_full, C = C_matrix)

ec |>
  select(measure, min, median, max, range_min, sd, iqr, moran_i) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 1))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Measure", "Min", "Median", "Max", "Range", "SD", "IQR",
                      "Moran's I"),
        caption = "Spread of the exposure. A narrow range means there is no contrast to detect, however precisely the coefficient is estimated.")

ec |>
  select(measure, starts_with("n_over"), starts_with("pct_pop_over")) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct"), \(x) fmt_pct(x))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Measure", "Areas >30 min", ">45 min", ">60 min",
                      "% pop >30 min", ">45 min", ">60 min"),
        caption = "Areas and population beyond clinically meaningful thresholds. 45 minutes is the DGR's own mothership centralisation criterion.")
```

```{r contrast-verdict, results="asis"}
hub <- ec[ec$measure == "t_hub_mean", ]
if (nrow(hub)) {
  n45 <- hub[["n_over_45"]]
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("\n> **Verdict.** Travel time to a thrombectomy hub spans %s to %s ",
           "minutes (range %s minutes, SD %s). %s areal unit(s) lie beyond the ",
           "45-minute mothership threshold, covering %s of the population.%s\n\n"),
    fmt_num(hub$min, 1), fmt_num(hub$max, 1), fmt_num(hub$range_min, 1),
    fmt_num(hub$sd, 1), fmt_n(n45), fmt_pct(hub[["pct_pop_over_45"]]),
    if (n45 == 0)
      paste0(" **No area in the study is beyond the threshold the regional",
             " network itself uses to define inadequate access.** The design",
             " cannot test the centralisation criterion, because the ATS",
             " Milano territory does not contain the contrast.")
    else ""
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("> The exposure has a Moran's I of %s, i.e. it is a smooth spatial ",
           "surface. It therefore competes directly with the BYM2 random ",
           "effect for the same variation — see §5.2.\n\n"),
    fmt_num(hub$moran_i, 3)))
}
```

# 5. Models

## 5.1 The raw association, before any model

```{r fig-raw, fig.cap="Cerebrovascular SMR against travel time to the nearest hub. Point size is the expected count, so the large points are the areas the model actually learns from."}
plot_tracer_raw(smr_geo_tracer, "t_hub_mean")
```

## 5.2 Road A — what is the exposure actually a proxy for?

A level-II centre is not only a thrombectomy centre. It provides neurosurgical
and neurocritical care, and that channel acts on haemorrhagic stroke — which is
the **majority** of premature cerebrovascular deaths here (see §2.1). The
mechanism written into the Methods was thrombectomy alone, which reaches only
a few per cent of this outcome; the neurosurgical channel reaches about half.

Organised stroke-unit care of any level also has better evidence for a
population mortality effect than thrombectomy specifically, so both destination
sets are fitted.

```{r exposure-table}
tracer_exposure_table |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, ci_low, ci_high), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3))) |>
  select(model, label, estimate, ci_low, ci_high, ess, rhat) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Destination set", "Term", "RR per SD", "2.5%", "97.5%",
                      "ESS", "R-hat"),
        caption = "Cerebrovascular mortality 0-74 against travel time to two different destination sets.")
```

## 5.3 Is the null real, or is the exposure unidentified?

The exposure is a smooth spatial surface and so is the BYM2 random effect. When
two terms describe the same variation, the data cannot say which owns it and
the covariate coefficient is pulled toward zero regardless of whether an effect
exists. Fitting the same tracer under three treatments of spatial structure
separates "no association" from "not identified".

**Watch the effective sample size**, not just the interval. A low ESS
concentrated on the exposure coefficient, while the intercept samples freely,
is the signature of a covariate trading off against the random effect.

```{r engine-table}
tracer_engine_table |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, ci_low, ci_high), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3))) |>
  select(model, label, estimate, ci_low, ci_high, ess, rhat) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Specification", "Term", "RR per SD", "2.5%", "97.5%",
                      "ESS", "R-hat"),
        caption = "The same tracer under three treatments of spatial structure.")
```

```{r engine-verdict, results="asis"}
te <- tracer_engine_table
g  <- te$estimate[grepl("GLM", te$model)]
b  <- te$estimate[te$model == "BYM2"]
if (length(g) && length(b)) {
  cat(if (abs(log(g)) > 2 * abs(log(b)))
    paste0("\n> **The association is much larger without the spatial term.** ",
           "That is an identification result, not a substantive one: the BYM2 ",
           "random effect is absorbing the travel-time gradient. Neither ",
           "estimate should be read as the effect of access; what the data ",
           "support is that the exposure and the spatial structure are not ",
           "separable at this resolution.\n\n")
  else
    paste0("\n> The estimate is stable across specifications, so the null is ",
           "not an artefact of the spatial term competing with the exposure.\n\n"))
}
```

## 5.4 The control panel

```{r control-table}
control_table |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, ci_low, ci_high), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3))) |>
  select(role, outcome, label, estimate, ci_low, ci_high, verdict) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Role", "Outcome", "Exposure", "RR per SD", "2.5%",
                      "97.5%", "Verdict"),
        caption = "Tracer and controls. The verdict column checks direction against the pre-specified expectation, not merely whether the interval clears the null.")
```

```{r control-expectations}
control_table |>
  select(role, expectation) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Role", "Pre-specified expectation"),
        caption = "Written before the estimates were seen.")
```

## 5.5 The coefficient in clinical units

"Per standard deviation" is not a unit anyone can act on, and it hides the
range-restriction problem: a small SD makes a null look like strong evidence
when it is really evidence about a contrast nobody cares about.

```{r mde}
mde <- mde_per_unit(control_fits$tracer, smr_geo_tracer, "t_hub_mean", per = 10)

mde |>
  mutate(across(c(sd_raw, rr, ci_low, ci_high, rules_out_above, p_direction),
                \(x) fmt_num(x, 3))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Variable", "Per (min)", "SD (min)", "RR", "2.5%",
                      "97.5%", "Rules out effects above", "P(direction)"),
        caption = "Tracer coefficient re-expressed per 10 minutes of additional travel time to a thrombectomy hub.")
```

```{r mde-prose, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf(
  paste0("\n> Each additional 10 minutes to a thrombectomy hub is associated ",
         "with a relative risk of %s (95%% CrI %s to %s) for cerebrovascular ",
         "mortality. The data rule out effects larger than about %s per 10 ",
         "minutes in either direction. Whether that is a useful null depends ",
         "entirely on §4: if the whole territory sits within %s minutes of a ",
         "hub, this interval is uninformative about the question the ",
         "centralisation policy actually poses.\n\n"),
  fmt_num(mde$rr, 3), fmt_num(mde$ci_low, 3), fmt_num(mde$ci_high, 3),
  fmt_pct(100 * (mde$rules_out_above - 1)),
  fmt_num(max(smr_geo_full$t_hub_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 0)
))
```

## 5.6 Convergence

```{r control-diag}
control_diagnostics |>
  mutate(across(c(rhat_max, rho), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3)),
         pct_divergent = fmt_pct(pct_divergent)) |>
  select(model, rhat_max, ess_min, n_divergent, pct_divergent, rho) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Divergent",
                      "% divergent", "rho"),
        caption = "A low minimum ESS concentrated on the exposure coefficient indicates weak identification rather than a sampler problem.")
```

# 6. Road B — all-age outcomes

The 75-year ceiling belongs to the OECD/Eurostat avoidability definition, not
to the clinical question. **An ischaemic stroke at 90 is as treatable as one at
60**, and excluding those events discards most of what the exposure could act
on. These outcomes go back to the register directly, standardised over the full
age range against the same population denominator.

## 6.1 Is there enough to model?

::: {.callout-important}
Read the verdict column before anything below it. A BYM2 fitted to a surface
that is zero across most units returns the prior, not the data — and it returns
it as a smooth, plausible-looking map.
:::

```{r feasibility}
outcome_feasibility_table |>
  mutate(
    outcome = recode(outcome,
                     i63    = "I63 cerebral infarction, all ages",
                     cvdall = "I60-I69 all cerebrovascular, all ages",
                     haem   = "I60-I62 haemorrhagic, under 75"),
    across(c(mean_per_area, median_per_area, median_expected), \(x) fmt_num(x, 1)),
    across(c(pct_zero, pct_expected_under5), \(x) fmt_pct(x))
  ) |>
  select(outcome, deaths, mean_per_area, median_per_area, max_per_area,
         n_zero, pct_zero, median_expected, verdict) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Outcome", "Deaths", "Mean/area", "Median/area",
                      "Max/area", "Areas with 0", "% zero", "Median expected",
                      "Verdict"),
        caption = "Feasibility of each candidate outcome at 279-area resolution. Compare against the 0-74 avoidable cerebrovascular outcome, which has 851 deaths.")
```

ggplot(d, aes(x = t_hub_mean, y = i63_smr)) +

# 7. Interpretation

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read the null carefully

A null tracer coefficient is consistent with at least four different states of
the world, and this design cannot fully separate them. State which one you
believe, and why, rather than reporting "no association".

1. **No effect.** Access to thrombectomy does not affect population-level
   cerebrovascular mortality in this territory.
2. **No contrast.** There is an effect, but every area is close enough that the
   study contains no exposure gradient to detect it with. §4 answers this
   directly.
3. **Wrong outcome.** Mortality is incidence times case fatality. Access can
   only move case fatality, and only for the thrombectomy-eligible subset —
   ischaemic strokes, presenting in window, large-vessel occlusion. Deaths from
   haemorrhagic stroke, deaths before contact with services, and long-run
   sequelae all sit in the numerator and dilute the signal toward zero.
4. **Not identified.** The exposure and the spatial random effect describe the
   same smooth variation. §5.2 addresses this.
:::

```{r nco-reading, results="asis"}
tr  <- control_table[control_table$role == "Tracer", ]
nco <- control_table[control_table$role == "Negative control outcome", ]

if (nrow(tr) && nrow(nco)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("\n**The negative control.** Travel time is associated with ",
           "all-cancer mortality at RR %s (%s to %s), against %s (%s to %s) ",
           "for the tracer. %s\n\n"),
    fmt_num(nco$estimate, 3), fmt_num(nco$ci_low, 3), fmt_num(nco$ci_high, 3),
    fmt_num(tr$estimate, 3), fmt_num(tr$ci_low, 3), fmt_num(tr$ci_high, 3),
    if (abs(log(nco$estimate)) > abs(log(tr$estimate)))
      paste0("The negative control association is **larger** than the tracer ",
             "association. Whatever travel time is measuring here, it is not ",
             "specific to time-critical care: it tracks something about area ",
             "character that also predicts cancer mortality. The tracer null ",
             "cannot be read as evidence about the stroke pathway until this ",
             "is explained.")
    else
      paste0("The negative control is smaller than the tracer association, ",
             "which is the pattern the design was built to detect.")
  ))
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Still open

The **negative control exposure** has not been chosen, so the panel has three
of its four slots filled. Without it, residual confounding by area type cannot
be assessed from the exposure side.
:::

# Appendix. Section-level routing

```{r section-summary}
stroke_times |>
  summarise(
    sections        = n(),
    population      = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    unreached       = sum(is.na(t_centre_min)),
    median_centre   = median(t_centre_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_hub      = median(t_hub_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_hub         = max(t_hub_min, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 1))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Census sections", "Population", "Unreached",
                      "Median to centre", "Median to hub", "Max to hub"),
        caption = "Routing at its native resolution, before aggregation to areal units.")
```

```{r dominant-hub}
stroke_area |>
  count(dominant_hub, name = "areas") |>
  arrange(desc(areas)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Dominant hub", "Areal units"),
        caption = "Which hub serves most of each area's population. A hub serving implausibly many or few units is worth checking against its coordinate in Table 1.")
```

```{r centroid-bias}
diag_stroke$centroid_bias |>
  head(15) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 1))) |>
  kable(caption = "Areas where routing from a centroid would have differed most from the population-weighted section mean.")
```
